rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī treats the challenge to name the things as evidence that the angels' preceding claim was false, while presenting the inference as a question.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { أنبئونى بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين } ( البقرة : 31 ) يدل على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes 2:33 to show that the angels had not known this before the episode and had doubted God's knowledge of all things.
rows.anchor: ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والارض وأعلم ما تبدون وما كنتم تكتمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation of the corruption forecast is unlikely because repeating an inspired fact would be pointless; he infers conjecture, forbidden by 17:36 and 10:36.
rows.anchor: فثبت أنهم قالوه عن الاستنباط والظن والقدح في الغير على سبيل الظن غير جائز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God addressed the angels who had been Iblīs's troops in the war against the jinn; their question about a corrupting successor drew God's anger, and they repented by admitting their ignorance.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : إن الله سبحانه وتعالى قال للملائكة

rows.speaker: الجن وقتادة
rows.claim: A report attributed to the jinn and Qatāda says the angels privately expected every new creature to be inferior to them; Adam's knowledge exposed that boast, so they repented and confessed ignorance.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الجن وقتادة أن الله تعالى لما أخذ في خلق آدم همست الملائكة فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some narrations add that God sent fire to burn the angels after they asked whether He would place a corruptor on earth.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أنهم لما قالوا أتجعل فيها ، أرسل الله عليهم نارا فأحرقتهم

rows.speaker: من تمسكوا بقصة هاروت وماروت
rows.claim: The account says Hārūt and Mārūt condemned human sins and prayed against people; God warned that human desires would make them disobey, but they claimed they would resist and were sent down for a test.
rows.anchor: تمسكوا بقصة هاروت وماروت وزعموا أنهما كانا ملكين من الملائكة

rows.speaker: من تمسكوا بقصة هاروت وماروت
rows.claim: In the story, Venus and her accompanying angel take human forms; the angels visit Venus, refuse sex unless they drink wine, then succumb to desire, and she imposes another condition.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إليهما إني لو ابتليتكما بما ابتليت به بني آدم من الشهوات لعصيتماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After giving the angels a general answer about the wisdom of creating Adam, God clarified it by displaying Adam's knowledge, exposing their limits and reinforcing the general answer with a specific one.
rows.anchor: أراد تعالى أن يزيدهم بيانا وأن يفصل لهم ذلك المجمل

rows.speaker: الأشعري والجبائي والكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿarī, al-Jubbāʾī, and al-Kaʿbī hold that all languages are divinely instituted: God creates necessary knowledge of expressions, meanings, and their assignment.
rows.anchor: قال الأشعري والجبائي والكعبي : اللغات كلها توقيفية . بمعنى أن الله تعالى خلق علما ضروريا

rows.speaker: الأشعري والجبائي والكعبي
rows.claim: They argue that the construction of teaching Adam the names implies those names already existed before the teaching, so language preceded it.
rows.anchor: وذلك يقتضي في تلك الأسماء أنها كانت أسماء قبل ذلك التعليم ، وإذا كان كذلك كانت اللغات حاصلة

rows.speaker: الأشعري والجبائي والكعبي
rows.claim: They argue that the angels had to recognize Adam's naming as correct for his challenge to prove his truth, implying that name-to-thing assignments predated his instruction.
rows.anchor: وذلك يقتضي أن يكون وضع تلك الأسماء لتلك المسميات متقدما على ذلك التعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that God could create necessary knowledge that some assigner had assigned these names to these things without revealing whether the assigner was God or people.
rows.anchor: بخلق العلم الضروري بأن واضعا وضع هذه الأسماء لهذه المسميات من غير تعيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers another objection by allowing that God addressed the angels through another medium, such as writing.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقال خاطب الملائكة بطريق آخر بالكتابة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers a third objection by saying God's prior will to assign words to meanings suffices for teaching to be attributed to the names.
rows.anchor: إرادة الله تعالى وضع تلك الألفاظ لتلك المعاني سابقة على التعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī postpones his answer to the fourth argument for later discussion.
rows.anchor: وعن الرابع : ماسيأتي بيانه إن شاء الله تعالى والله تعالى أعلم .

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: Some interpret the names as the qualities, attributes, and properties of things, reasoning from the derivation of ism from sima, a mark that identifies an essence.
rows.anchor: أي علمه صفات الأشياء ونعوتها وخواصها والدليل عليه أن الاسم اشتقاقه إما من السمة أو من السمو

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: They also derive ism from sumu, elevation: a thing's evidence stands above it, and knowledge of evidence comes before knowledge of what it proves.
rows.anchor: وإن كان من السمو فكذلك لأن دليل الشيء كالمرتفع على ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: They argue that grammarians' restriction of ism to particular word forms is a later convention and cannot rule out the broader meaning of qualities.
rows.anchor: ولكن ذلك عرف حادث لا اعتبار به

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: They prefer realities over labels because knowledge of things' realities is more meritorious, fitting a passage meant to display Adam's superiority.
rows.anchor: أن الفضيلة في معرفة حقائق الأشياء أكثر من الفضيلة في معرفة أسمائها

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: They argue that a challenge should test a capacity the audience can in principle share: language is learned only through instruction, whereas reason can attain knowledge of realities.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن العقل لا طريق له إلى معرفة اللغات البتة : بل ذلك لا يحصل إلا بالتعليم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand the names as names for all created kinds, in all the different languages spoken by Adam's descendants, including Arabic, Persian, and Greek.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو الشمهور أن المراد أسماء كل ما خلق الله من أجناس المحدثات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this account Adam's children spoke all these languages; after his death they spread out, each language prevailed in different groups, and generations forgot the others, explaining linguistic diversity.
rows.anchor: فلما مات آدم وتفرق ولده في نواحي العالم تكلم كل واحد منهم بلغة معينة

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The grammarians of meaning posit an ellipsis: God taught Adam either names of the referents or the referents of the names; they prefer the former because 2:33 says to tell their names.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : قوله تعالى : { وعلم ءادم الاسماء } لا بد فيه من إضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the displayed set included non-rational things, the masculine plural pronoun is used because rational angels, humans, and jinn occur among them and the more complete category governs Arabic agreement.
rows.anchor: كان في جملتها الملائكة والإنس والجن وهم العقلاء ، فغلب الأكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God's request of the angels proves the permissibility of assigning an impossible task is weak: the request rebuked them while God knew they could not answer, as the challenge clause shows.
rows.anchor: لأنه تعالى إنما استنبأهم مع علمه تعالى بعجزهم على سبيل التبكيت

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites say Adam's knowledge of the names was a miracle that proved his prophethood at that moment; Rāzī considers commissioning him to Eve most likely and does not rule out the angels as addressees.
rows.anchor: المسألة الرابعة : قالت المعتزلة : إن ما ظهر من آدم عليه السلام من علمه بالأسماء معجزة دالة على نبوته

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their proof is that the knowledge violated ordinary patterns, making it a miracle and therefore evidence that Adam was a messenger then.
rows.anchor: بأن حصول ذلك العلم له ناقض للعادة فوجب أن يكون معجزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī objects that knowledge of a language is ordinary when God teaches it and its absence is ordinary when He does not, so Adam's knowledge need not violate custom.
rows.anchor: لأن حصول العلم باللغة لمن علمه الله تعالى وعدم حصوله لمن لم يعلمه الله ليس بناقض للعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī poses a dilemma: if the angels knew the name-to-thing mappings, they could name the objects too and Adam's distinction would disappear; if not, how could they verify his correctness?
rows.anchor: فإن علموا ذلك فقد قدروا على أن يذكروا أسماء تلك المسميات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed solution is that different angelic classes knew different languages; Adam recited them all, so each class verified its own language while all angels together could not produce the complete set, making it miraculous.
rows.anchor: ربما كان لكل صنف من أصناف الملائكة لغة من هذه اللغات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second solution is that God gave the angels evidence of Adam's truth before they heard the names, so they recognized his correctness and the miracle when he spoke.
rows.anchor: إنه تعالى عرفهم قبل أن سمعوا من آدم عليه السلام تلك الأسماء ما استدلوا به على صدق آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if Adam performed an extraordinary act, Rāzī says it could have been a saintly wonder or a prophetic precursor, both allowed in his theological school, so the issue depends on those doctrines.
rows.anchor: فلم لا يجوز أن يكون ذلك من باب الكرامات أو من باب الإرهاص وهما عندنا جائزان

rows.speaker: من قطع بأنه عليه السلام ما كان نبيا في ذلك الوقت
rows.claim: Those denying prophethood then argue that if Adam were already a prophet, his later agreed-upon lapse would be a major sin after prophethood, deserving disgrace and incompatible with prophets; therefore it preceded prophethood.
rows.anchor: واحتج من قطع بأنه عليه السلام ما كان نبيا في ذلك الوقت بوجوه : أحدها : أنه لو كان نبيا

rows.speaker: من قطع بأنه عليه السلام ما كان نبيا في ذلك الوقت
rows.claim: They argue that a messenger must have an addressee, but none fits: under the Muʿtazilite ranking angels outrank humans, Eve alone existed and was addressed directly, no jinn were in heaven, and a messenger without a recipient serves no purpose.
rows.anchor: لو كان رسولا في ذلك الوقت لكان إما أن يكون مبعوثا إلى أحد أو لا يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the argument that Adam had no possible recipient is not especially strong.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه ليس في غاية القوة

rows.speaker: من قطع بأنه عليه السلام ما كان نبيا في ذلك الوقت
rows.claim: They infer from 2:37 that God chose Adam only after his lapse; since selection and messengership go together, he was not a messenger beforehand, citing 6:124.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : قوله تعالى : { ثم اجتباه ربه } فهذه الآية دل على أنه تعالى إنما اجتباه بعد الزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading asks the angels to name the objects if they know they can report truthfully.
rows.anchor: معناه أعلموني أسماء هؤلاء إن علمتم أنكم تكونون صادقين في ذلك الأعلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading commands them to report nothing but truth; it emphasizes their incapacity by making them recognize that they cannot truthfully answer or access the names.
rows.anchor: معناه أخبروني ولا تقولوا إلا حقا وصدقا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd take the condition to mean: if you are truthful that no creature is burdened with worship except one that you can perform.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading challenges the angels to name the objects if their claim is true that God creates no creature more knowledgeable than them.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم صادقين في قولكم إني لم أخلق خلقا إلا كنتم أعلم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves knowledge's excellence: God displayed the wisdom of Adam's creation by displaying his knowledge, which would be the highest excellence if anything better existed He would have displayed that instead.
rows.anchor: ما أظهر كمال حكمته في خلقه آدم عليه السلام إلا بأن أظهر علمه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil identifies four Qurʾānic meanings of wisdom: Qurʾānic admonitions, understanding and knowledge, prophethood, and the Qurʾān itself; Rāzī says all reduce to knowledge.
rows.anchor: ما يروى عن مقاتل : أنه قال : تفسر الحكمة في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān calls human knowledge little and worldly enjoyment little; since the world's finite extent, number, and duration contrast with knowledge and its rewards, the unnamed measure of knowledge must be vast.
rows.anchor: وسمى الدنيا بأسرها قليلا { قل متاع الدنيا قليل } ( النساء : 77 ) فما سماه قليلا لا يمكننا أن ندرك كميته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second proof is 39:9: scripture's contrasts between impure and pure, blind and seeing, darkness and light, Paradise and Fire, and shade and heat ultimately reflect the difference between learned and ignorant.
rows.anchor: وإذا تأملت وجدت كل ذلك مأخوذا من الفرق بين العالم والجاهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third proof is 4:59: the strongest interpretation of those in authority identifies them as scholars, since rulers must obey scholars, not conversely.
rows.anchor: والمراد من أولى الأمر العلماء في أصح الأقوال لأن الملوك يجب عليهم طاعة العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture places scholars second beside God and the angels in 3:18 and beside God and the Messenger in 4:59, then gives them first place among humans in 3:7 and 13:43.
rows.anchor: ثم انظر إلى هذه المرتبة فإنه تعالى ذكر العالم في موضعين من كتابه في المرتبة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth proof is 58:11, which says God raises believers and those given knowledge in rank; this section begins the four groups by citing the ranks of the believers at Badr.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى ذكر الدرجات لأربعة أصناف . وألها : للمؤمنين من أهل بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī ranks four groups named in scripture: Badr believers, fighters, the righteous, and scholars; because scholars receive ranks above the other groups, he concludes they are the best people.
rows.anchor: ثم فضل العلماء على جميع الأصناف بدرجات ، فوجب أن يكون العلماء أفضل الناس .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifth proof is that only scholars truly fear God; Rāzī lists their five scriptural traits as faith, monotheistic witness, weeping, humility, and reverent fear.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى وصف العلماء في كتابه بخمس مناقب ، أحدها : الإيمان

rows.speaker: ثابت عن أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports from the Prophet that learners are among those freed from Hell: each step to a scholar earns worship and a city in Paradise, the earth seeks forgiveness for the learner, and angels attest their freedom.
rows.anchor: أحدها : روى ثابت عن أنس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من أحب أن ينظر إلى عتقاء الله من النار

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that a person seeking knowledge for other than God will ultimately be brought to God by it; knowledge sought for God is like day-long fasting and night-long prayer, and one learned chapter outweighs a mountain of gold spent in God's way.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : عن أنس قال : قال عليه السلام : ( من طلب العلم لغير الله لم يخرج من الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports from the Prophet that one who dies seeking knowledge to revive Islam will stand one degree below the prophets in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : عن الحسن مرفوعا ) من جاءه الموت وهو يطلب العلم ليحيى به الإسلام

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī reports that on Judgment Day God singles out scholars, saying He placed His light and knowledge among them because He knew them and not to punish them, and then forgives them.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أبو موسى الأشعري مرفوعا ( يبعث الله العباد يوم القيامة ثم يميز العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that when a teacher of good dies, the birds of the sky, animals of the land, and fish of the sea mourn him.
rows.anchor: وخامسها : قال عليه السلام : ( معلم الخير إذا مات بكى عليه طير السماء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that praying behind a scholar is like praying behind a prophet.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : أبو هريرة مرفوعا ( من صلى خلف عالم من العلماء فكأنما صلى خلف نبي من الأنبياء )

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that a scholar outranks a worshipper by seventy degrees, each a seventy-year ride apart, because a scholar recognizes and removes innovations that a worshipper misses.
rows.anchor: وسابعها : ابن عمر مرفوعا ( فضل العالم على العابد بسبعين درجة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports the Prophet's prayer for mercy upon his successors, identified as those who revive his Sunna and teach it to God's servants.
rows.anchor: وثامنها : الحسن مرفوعا قال عليه السلام : ( رحمة الله على خلفائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report equates seeking knowledge to correct falsehood or guide people from misguidance with forty years of worship.
rows.anchor: من خرج يطلب بابا من العلم ليرد به باطلا إلى حق أو ضلالا إلى هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet sent ʿAlī to Yemen, he said that guiding one person is better than everything on which the sun rises or sets.
rows.anchor: وعاشرها : قال عليه السلام لعلي حين بعثه إلى اليمن ( لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that one who seeks knowledge to teach people for God's sake receives the reward of seventy prophets.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر : ابن مسعود مرفوعا ( من طلب العلم ليحدث به الناس ابتغاء وجه الله

rows.speaker: عامر الجهني
rows.claim: ʿĀmir al-Juhanī reports that the ink of a knowledge-seeker and a martyr's blood are weighed equally at Judgment Day; another version says scholars' ink outweighs the blood.
rows.anchor: الثاني عشر : عامر الجهني مرفوعا ( يؤتى بمداد طالب العلم ودم الشهيد يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو وافد الليثي
rows.claim: Abū Wāqid al-Laythī reports a Muslim narration about three men at the Prophet's gathering: God shelters the one who joins, is gracious to the shy one who stays behind, and turns away from the one who leaves.
rows.anchor: الثالث عشر : أبو وافد الليثي : أنه عليه السلام بينما هو جالس والناس معه إذ أقبل ثلاثة نفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed saying compares scholars' care for pupils with parental care: parents protect against worldly fire and harms, while scholars protect against Hell and the terrors of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: العالم أرأف بالتلميذ من الأب والأم لأن الآباء والأمهات يحفظونه من نار الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Asked how he gained knowledge, Ibn Masʿūd says it came through a questioning tongue and an understanding heart.
rows.anchor: بم وجدت هذا العلم : قال بلسان سؤول ، وقلب عقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed maxim advises asking questions with a fool's boldness and retaining knowledge with the wise person's care.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم سل مسألة الحمقى ، واحفظ حفظ الأكياس

rows.speaker: مصعب بن الزبير
rows.claim: Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr tells his son to learn: with wealth, knowledge adorns him; without wealth, knowledge itself becomes his wealth.
rows.anchor: مصعب بن الزبير قال لابنه : يا بني تعلم العلم فإن كان لك مال كان العلم لك جمالا

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī says there is no good in withholding knowledge, just as there is no good in speaking from ignorance.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب : لا خير في الصمت عن العلم كما لا خير في الكلام عن الجهل

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some discerning scholars divide scholars into three: one knows God but not His commands, one knows His commands but not God, and one knows both God and His commands.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المحققين : العلماء ثلاثة عالم بالله غير عالم بأمر الله
